                <h3>Kane's Method</h3>
                <p class="resource-description">
                  Educational video explaining Kane's method, a powerful technique for deriving equations of motion 
                  for mechanical systems. Kane's method provides an efficient alternative to Lagrangian mechanics 
                  for analyzing multibody systems and is particularly useful for systems with constraints. This 
                  method is relevant for understanding the dynamics of complex mechanical systems like the golf swing.
                </p>

                          allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture" 
                          allowfullscreen></iframe>
                </div>
              </div>
              <div class="resource-content">
                <h3>Intermediate Axis Theorem (Secondary Axis Instability)</h3>
                <p class="resource-description">
                  Demonstration of the intermediate axis theorem, also known as secondary axis instability or the 
                  tennis racket theorem. This fundamental principle of rigid body dynamics explains why rotation 
                  about the intermediate moment of inertia axis is unstable, which has important implications for 
                  understanding golf club dynamics and shaft behavior during the swing.
                </p>
                <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1VPfZ_XzisU"
                   class="resource-link"
                   target="_blank"
                   rel="noopener">
                  Watch Video →
                </a>
              </div>
            </div>

                          title="Dead Fish Swimming Upstream - YouTube Video"

                          allowfullscreen></iframe>
                </div>
              </div>
              <div class="resource-content">
                <h3>Dead Fish Swimming Upstream</h3>
                <p class="resource-description">
                  A fascinating fluid dynamics demonstration showing how a dead fish can swim upstream due to 
                  vortex-induced motion. This phenomenon illustrates important principles of fluid-structure 
                  interactions and passive dynamics, which have relevance to understanding how objects move 
                  through fluids and how passive forces can drive motion in biomechanical systems.
                </p>

<script>
// Track video history in localStorage
document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function() {
  const videosHistoryList = document.getElementById('videos-history-list');
  if (!videosHistoryList) return;

  const VIDEO_PAGES = [
    'resources-videos.html'
  ];

  function updateVideosHistory() {
    let history = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('affinedrift_videos_history') || '[]');
    
    const currentPage = {
      title: document.title.replace(' - AffineDrift', '').replace('AffineDrift - ', ''),
      url: window.location.pathname.split('/').pop() || 'resources-videos.html'
    };

    if (VIDEO_PAGES.includes(currentPage.url)) {
      history = history.filter(item => item.url !== currentPage.url);
      history.unshift(currentPage);
      history = history.slice(0, 10);
      localStorage.setItem('affinedrift_videos_history', JSON.stringify(history));
    }

    if (history.length === 0) {
      videosHistoryList.innerHTML = '<li class="history-empty">No recent videos yet</li>';
      return;
    }

        videosHistoryList.innerHTML = '';
    history.forEach(item => {
      const li = document.createElement('li');
      const a = document.createElement('a');
      a.href = typeof item.url === "string" && !item.url.replace(/[\x00-\x20]/g, "").toLowerCase().startsWith("javascript:") ? item.url : "#";
      a.textContent = item.title;
      li.appendChild(a);
      videosHistoryList.appendChild(li);
    });
  }

  updateVideosHistory();
});
</script>
